speaker: tiffanyspeir
text: Good evening, Mr. Mayor, members of the council, Tiffany Speer here from Community and Economic Development. I'm going to share my screen. So as the mayor just mentioned, this is related to the population and employment target process that happens periodically, starting with the state and with the Puget Sound Regional Council and eventually coming down to the Pierce County itself and the cities within it to decide the population and employment targets to assign to each jurisdiction and then for them to work on that for the next number of years. In this case, we're talking about 2044 as the new employment and population target horizon. So the Puget Sound Regional Council last year adopted Vision 2050, which includes multi-county planning policies and also what's called the regional growth strategy. So for all four counties covered by PSRC, King, Pierce, Snohomish, and Kitsap, there are a targeted number of people and jobs to various levels or sizes of cities. In this case, City of Lakewood is considered a core city. There's 16 of those total in all four of the counties put together. And of those 16, the amount intended by Vision 2050 to come to Pierce County is 85,000 people and 44,000 jobs. So along with Lakewood, the other core cities within Pierce County are University Place, Puyallup, and then Auburn and the parts that come down from King County and come into Pierce County. So all four of those cities again are intended, or I should say are expected to absorb some portion of the 85,000 people and 44,000 jobs. Pierce County is in charge of shepherding this process through and ultimately the Pierce County Council takes action to adopt an ordinance that sets population and employment targets. Last year, Pierce County hired AHBL as a consultant, which in turn developed two initial population targets for Lakewood. And the target horizon is 2044 for this. The two potential numbers were 88,758 and 80,488. And there were two different theories behind those numbers, which is why they ended up different. The city of Lakewood itself responded to those two by looking at its own historical growth trends, and also the limits on land availability and densification possibility, and responded back with an initial request that the 2044 population target for Lakewood be set at 68,000. Once we got the results out of the 2020 census though, the landscape changed a little bit. Instead of the estimated population of about 60,000 for Lakewood in the year 2020, it was shown through the census that it was higher than that at 63,612. So what was then done is taking a look at the number of people per year since the year 20, I'm sorry, since the year 2000, and then moving to 2020, how many per year came in, you see 545 people per year in that timeframe. We took that as a starting point and we said, okay, if that is the annual growth rate that we're going to continue to see in the city of Lakewood, and we've moved that forward from the year 2021 to 2024, then what we're going to be seeing is a proposed population of 76,692. So this is based on both the number from the census, and then the real life 545 person per year average from the years 2010 through 2020 in the city of Lakewood. That's where the 76,692 came from. If we were to take a look at the growth and density that are planned for within the downtown sub area and the Lakewood station sub area, you would see it was planned for at kind of the mid level of densities that is possible within the zones within those sub areas. If you were to go and say, rather than that mid level build out, we're going to see the maximum available density build out, you would end up with 806 additional housing units in downtown and almost 495 in the Lakewood station district. These two numbers added together are this 1,298. If you go back to the amount that's targeted for the city of Lakewood under 76,692 total, these two numbers together brings you very close to the 2044 target. If an additional 11,000, I'm sorry, 11 housing units per year happened in other parts of the city, the 76,692 would be met. One note here is that Pierce County has responded back after seeing the census number with a number that's about 3,500 higher than what the city has requested. So at this point, Pierce County is talking about 80,274 as the 2044 target. What then is the outcome? What is the next step? If Lakewood says, we're going to assume a higher densification within the two sub areas as they build out, which is a not unreasonable assumption, given the much faster than expected interest in redeveloping, particularly the Lakewood station district, we may well see these numbers be hit even without significant growth in other parts of the city. Then you may see the city hit either 76,692 or somewhere up to and including 80,274 by the year 2044. This would be compliance, if you will, by the city of Lakewood to what Pierce County will in the near future be adopting as the new updated population and employment ordinance. However, there's still this total number of people and jobs that were assigned back with the multi-county planning policies in vision 2050. What will happen at that point is that Auburn, Lakewood, Puyallup and University Place will all be involved in discussions at the Puget Sound Regional Council level regarding the amount of growth that they're planning for. Given how this number of 76,692 was arrived at and the math behind it, we're feeling pretty confident that this is justifiable. And in fact, it is also reasonable that Lakewood could hit this 80,000 number given the two sub areas and how they will be densifying in the relatively near future. So just understanding that there will be some questions and discussions about how all four core cities in Pierce County are planning for their total number. This is putting Lakewood in a pretty good position with both the Pierce County Regional Council and then ultimately Puget Sound Regional Council. So with that, I am happy to answer questions, but the next steps will be the Pierce County Regional Council will start to discuss this either in December or perhaps early 2022.
